clue.text: Beef with teacher — access to computer not good

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: not tells us the good letter is to be left out of the computer word

parts.note: a login is how you gain access to a computer

explanation.surface: A complaint that a teacher can't get onto the computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' reads as a grievance, but it is the meat. 'not' drops the G for good, leaving LOIN, a cut of meat in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef from the loin of the animal.

clue.text: Grand — United lost!

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds
united things are made one

explanation.surface: A football fan's cry of dismay that United have been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club, but here it means made one, ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lost has disappeared, so it is gone: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fancy quietly going home at end of evening? Lovely!

indicators.note: going says the quiet letter departs from the fancy word

parts.note: a penchant is a fancy or liking for something
P, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of evening

explanation.surface: Someone imagines slipping off home quietly at the close of an evening, and finds the idea delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes P out of PENCHANT, leaving ENCHANT; then IN and G from the end of 'evening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting charms and delights you, so it is lovely in the admiring sense.

clue.text: Extra studies hold up government-appointed 'expert'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the held letters read from bottom to top
the words Extra studies hold the answer's letters within them

explanation.surface: Extra studies hold up a government expert's appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' finds RAST across 'extRA STudies'; 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar is a British media term for an official appointed by government to lead on one issue, such as a drugs tsar; the quotes mock the expertise.

clue.text: I agree with cutting trees

indicators.note: the with letter is cutting into the agreeing word, splitting it

parts.note: yes is what you say to agree

explanation.surface: Someone agrees with a plan to cut down trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' places W inside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are evergreen conifers often found in churchyards, so they are trees.

clue.text: Name poses problem at Chinese border — might this enable access?

indicators.note: a problem with the words suggests they are in disorder and need rearranging
border here is the edge of the word Chinese, its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone's name causes trouble at a Chinese frontier crossing, and they wonder what would get them through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges NAMEPOSES; 'border' adds the last letter E of 'Chinese'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale of Ali Baba, the magic words open the robbers' cave, so they grant access.

clue.text: Roman occasionally loud, unfortunately, but rarely wicked

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have come out badly and need putting right
occasionally takes only every other letter of loud

explanation.surface: A Roman who is now and then noisy, which is a pity, though seldom actually bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives LU from 'loud'; 'unfortunately' rearranges ROMAN plus LU. 'rarely' flags that the word is uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoral is a rare word for lacking or outside morality; the clue's rarely marks how seldom it is used.

clue.text: Cast aside — is not happy on the surface

indicators.note: on the surface puts the is letters near the top of the gloomy word, just under its first letter

parts.note: to feel down is to be not happy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who looks cheerful but is unhappy underneath is cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy on the surface' suggests a cheerful front; instead 'on the surface' puts IS near the top of the gloomy word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to reject or repudiate them, casting them aside.

clue.text: Lazy start — sweethearts turn over and don't get up

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the turn word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a spin is a turn

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of Lazy

parts.note: read as sweet hearts: the two central letters of sweet

explanation.surface: A lazy morning: lovers roll over in bed instead of rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweethearts' must be split into sweet hearts, the middle pair of 'sweet'. 'start' takes the first letter of 'Lazy', and 'over' has the turn word covering both.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is to stay in bed past the usual hour, not getting up.

clue.text: They're blown away by bubbly person Helen used regularly

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for away in sports fixture lists

indicators.note: bubbly suggests effervescent letters fizzing into a new order
used regularly picks every other letter of Helen, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A lively Helen is so impressive she blows people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown away' looks like a phrase, but 'away' is split off as A. 'used regularly' keeps HLN, the odd letters of 'Helen', which 'bubbly' mixes with 'person'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpenhorns are long wooden horns played by Alpine herdsmen, wind instruments one blows.

clue.text: Queen of Jordan once reflecting on men

indicators.note: reflecting means the word on is seen as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: taken as written
OR, other ranks, is a military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A former Jordanian queen thinks back on the men in her life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' would usually mean placed after, but here it is fodder: 'reflecting' turns it round. 'men' is other ranks, the army's ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Noor, American-born widow of King Hussein, was the consort of Jordan until 1999.

clue.text: Right way to enter — take note

indicators.note: to enter has the way letters going into the legal word

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: Instructions on the correct way in, with a reminder to remember them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is not R here but a lien, a legal claim on property. 'to enter' sends the way abbreviation into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to pay attention or heed, taking note of what is said.

clue.text: Duck for us — maintaining standard in restaurant

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the duck word keeps the standard inside it

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
par is a standard level or norm
something for us is ours, hence our

explanation.surface: Someone orders duck at a restaurant that keeps up its standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is not O for zero but a species of duck. 'maintaining' has it hold the golf standard inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea parlour is a small eatery serving tea and light meals, a modest kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Win heart cavorting naked?

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Could you win someone's heart by prancing about with no clothes on?
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an idiom for being nude, without clothing.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a problem or point of dispute
a formal word for a person's offspring

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a matter in dispute and, in legal language, descendants or offspring.

clue.text: Linnaeus maybe wrong in principle — nothing to prevent one seeing clearly

indicators.note: in puts the wrong mark within the principle word

parts.note: the Tao is the guiding principle in Chinese philosophy
an X is the mark for a wrong answer
no means none, nothing
to mist, as glasses do, prevents one seeing clearly

explanation.surface: A judgment that the great botanist was wrong in principle, with nothing obscuring the view.
explanation.walkthrough: The principle is the Tao of Chinese philosophy, and 'wrong' is the cross for a wrong answer; 'in' sets the cross inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Linnaeus devised the binomial system for naming species, the classic example of a classifier of organisms.

clue.text: Intelligence attracts me, Alexa — opus is fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful and unreal, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells Amazon's voice assistant Alexa that its work is wonderful, because cleverness turns them on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges ALEXA OPUS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapiosexual is someone who finds intelligence the most sexually attractive quality in a partner.

clue.text: Nice one! Actor Martin ultimately perfect for Shaggy

parts.note: un is French for one, as spoken in Nice
Martin Kemp is an actor, once of Spandau Ballet and EastEnders

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of perfect

explanation.surface: Praise for actor Martin, perfect casting as a shaggy character.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so its 'one' is UN. Martin Kemp is a British actor known from the soap EastEnders.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or appearance is untidy and dishevelled, which is what shaggy describes.

clue.text: Secret place Oscar's approaching

parts.note: a closet is a small private room, a secret place
Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: Oscar's hiding place is getting near.
explanation.definitionFit: Being close to something means being near or approaching it.

clue.text: Catch fish after net's torn

indicators.note: after places the fishing word following the torn net
a torn net is ripped apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fisherman tries to catch fish with a ripped net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' scrambles 'net' into ENT. 'fish' is a verb, to angle, not a noun, and 'after' sets it behind ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle something is to snare it in a mesh or tangle, so to catch it.

clue.text: That is poor, rounding on Brydon's latest impressions

indicators.note: on means the following letters are placed after the Brydon letter
latest picks the last letter of Brydon's name

parts.note: IE, id est, is the abbreviation for that is

indicators.note: rounding means turning round, so the poor word is read backwards

parts.note: ill, as in poor health, means poor

explanation.surface: A verdict that a comedian's latest impressions are poor; Rob Brydon is famed for his impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' turns the word for poor around to make LLI. 'on' sets this after the last letter of Brydon. 'impressions' sounds like mimicry but means engraved prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Nielli are designs engraved in metal and filled with black alloy; prints taken from such plates are also called nielli, so impressions.

clue.text: Most of celebrity magazine's awful

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun used loosely: something that is hell is awful

indicators.note: most of means the magazine's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that a celebrity magazine is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity gossip magazine; 'Most of' drops its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something was hell means it was dreadful, an informal way of calling it awful.

clue.text: "Compile? It's easy!" (He's looking for an argument)

indicators.note: easy suggests relaxed, loose letters that can be shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boastful claim that compiling crosswords is simple, from someone spoiling for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easy' rearranges COMPILE ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemicist writes or speaks in fierce controversy, always seeking debate and dispute.

clue.text: One's spent after exercise like this

indicators.note: after puts the like-this word following the exercise letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: After a workout, one feels exhausted like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' looks like tiredness, but the definition is money: a peso is a coin one spends.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency unit of Mexico and other countries, so one is spent as money.

clue.text: See nothing overcoming intelligence

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: overcoming read as coming over means the nothing word is turned round

parts.note: FA, from sweet FA, is British slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Failing to notice anything beats being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' turns FA into AF. Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all. 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang (loaf of bread, head) for think.
explanation.definitionFit: Your loaf is your head in rhyming slang, and so your brains or common sense.

clue.text: Cabbage and pastry? That's not unknown

indicators.note: not says the unknown letter is absent from the pastry word

parts.note: choux is a light pastry used for eclairs
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A curious pairing of cabbage and pastry, which is a familiar combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops X from CHOUX.
explanation.definitionFit: Chou is French for cabbage, used in English for a cabbage or a cabbage-shaped rosette.

clue.text: Old power in America is surprisingly regressive

indicators.note: regressive says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the old power is held inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something in America is unexpectedly backward-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks letters within 'americA IS SURPrisingly', AISSURP; 'regressive' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a powerful German kingdom and state that dominated central Europe until 1947.

clue.text: Runs in, sees displays

indicators.note: in places the runs letter inside the seeing word

parts.note: to spot is to see
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs in and watches what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places R inside SPOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to wear or display it proudly, as in sporting a new hat.
